hints: Translate the two polynomial statements into $p(3)=0$ and $p'(3)=72$ using the factor and remainder theorems.
Differentiate $p(x)$ before substituting $x=3$ into each condition.
Form the two linear equations in $a$ and $b$, then solve them simultaneously and verify both original conditions.
walkthrough:
Apply the factor theorem with $x = 3$ since $(x - 3)$ is a factor of $p(x) = 6x^3 + ax^2 + bx + 9$:
$$p(3) = 0$$
$$6(3)^3 + a(3)^2 + b(3) + 9 = 0$$
$$6(27) + 9a + 3b + 9 = 0$$
$$162 + 9a + 3b + 9 = 0$$
$$9a + 3b + 171 = 0 \implies 9a + 3b = -171$$
$$\text{Divide throughout by } 3: \quad 3a + b = -57 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

Differentiate $p(x)$ using the power rule to find $p'(x)$:
$$p'(x) = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[6x^3 + ax^2 + bx + 9] = 18x^2 + 2ax + b$$

Subtract equation (1) from equation (2) to solve for $a$:
$$(6a + b) - (3a + b) = -90 - (-57)$$
$$3a = -90 + 57 = -33$$
$$a = \dfrac{-33}{3} = -11$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Factor Theorem: Substitutes $x=3$ into p and/or p′ and applies $p(3)=0$, $p'(3)=72$. $a=-11$, $b=-24$. The solved value is a=−11, b = −24.

hints: Insert the coefficients found in part (a), then divide $p(x)$ by the known factor $x-3$.
Factorise the resulting quadratic by splitting its middle term or matching two binomial factors.
Multiply the three factors mentally to check the leading coefficient, constant term, and signs.
walkthrough:
Write down the cubic polynomial with the evaluated coefficients:
$$p(x) = 6x^3 - 11x^2 - 24x + 9$$

Divide $p(x)$ by the known factor $(x - 3)$ using algebraic long division or equating coefficients:
$$\text{Set } 6x^3 - 11x^2 - 24x + 9 = (x - 3)(6x^2 + kx - 3)$$
$$\text{Comparing } x^2 \text{ terms: } -18 + k = -11 \implies k = 7$$
$$\text{Verification on } x \text{ terms: } -3k - 3 = -3(7) - 3 = -21 - 3 = -24 \quad \text{(consistent)}$$
$$p(x) = (x - 3)(6x^2 + 7x - 3)$$

Factorise the quadratic factor $6x^2 + 7x - 3$:
$$\text{Product } = 6 \times (-3) = -18, \quad \text{Sum } = +7 \implies \text{factors are } +9 \text{ and } -2$$
$$6x^2 + 9x - 2x - 3 = 3x(2x + 3) - 1(2x + 3) = (2x + 3)(3x - 1)$$

State the complete linear factorisation of $p(x)$:
$$p(x) = (x - 3)(2x + 3)(3x - 1)$$

ai_rubric.Polynomial Factorisation: Divides by $x-3$ or equates $(x-3)(6x^2+Ax+B)$, using a,b, to determine the quadratic. $(x-3)(6x^2+7x-3)$. p(x) = (x−3)(2x+3)(3x−1). p(x) = (x−3)(2x+3)(3x−1).

hints: Use the three linear factors from part (b) to list the three distinct zeros in increasing order.
Create a sign chart for the product across the four intervals determined by those zeros.
Select only the intervals where the product is negative, and exclude every zero because the inequality is strict.
walkthrough:
Find the three roots of $p(x) = 0$ from the factors in part (b):
$$x - 3 = 0 \implies x = 3$$
$$2x + 3 = 0 \implies 2x = -3 \implies x = -\dfrac{3}{2}$$
$$3x - 1 = 0 \implies 3x = 1 \implies x = \dfrac{1}{3}$$

Order the roots along the real number line to define four test intervals:
$$-\dfrac{3}{2} < \dfrac{1}{3} < 3$$

State the solution set for the strict inequality $p(x) < 0$:
$$x < -\dfrac{3}{2} \quad \text{or} \quad \dfrac{1}{3} < x < 3$$

ai_rubric.Solving Inequalities: Gives one final region, $x<-3/2$ or $1/3<x<3$, using the final two factors (not $x-3$). x < −3/2 or 1/3 < x < 3. x < −3/2 or 1/3 < x < 3.
